For fixed hidden vectors, g(x,y)=2σ(aᵀx+bᵀy+c) is input-dependent modulation, but its logit is additive. Mathematical implication: changing x cannot reverse the gate’s ordering of two lagged vectors y₁,y₂; that ordering depends only on bᵀ(y₁−y₂). It therefore cannot directly express general pairwise compatibility or sign-agreement/XOR matching. A bilinear logit xᵀWy, or a learned interaction term wᵀ(x⊙y), permits context-dependent ordering. Sigmoid introduces nonlinear coupling, and multiplying features by the gate creates interactions downstream, so describing the entire network as interaction-free would overstate the limitation. One scalar also rescales every channel identically.

Relevant temporal studies: [Wu et al., ICLR 2019](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1901.10430) compare static LightConv with input-dependent DynamicConv: 28.9 versus 29.7 BLEU on WMT English–German. DynamicConv predicts kernels from the current state alone, illustrating that adaptivity does not require explicit pairwise matching. [Dauphin et al., ICML 2017](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/dauphin17a/dauphin17a.pdf), §§5.2–5.3, compare causal GLUs against ungated, linear and bilinear layers; their bilinear layers are feature products, not bilinear pairwise gate logits. [Gated Temporal Diffusion, ECCV 2024](https://www.ecva.net/papers/eccv_2024/papers/07244.pdf), Table 3, ablates dilated temporal gating against gate removal, nondilated gates, manual masks and channel-only reweighting.

Useful control: retrain the same NextItNet with g=2σ(c), learning one input-independent scalar per corresponding layer/lag; also test g=1. These retain one jointly trained predictor/category. [Chen et al., CVPR 2020](https://arxiv.org/html/1912.03458v2), Table 3, replace dynamic attention with uniform kernel averaging, but this is an inference intervention on a trained dynamic model—not a retrained static control. Distinguish these tests; none establishes an Amazon HR@10 gain.
